The **Suzuki-Miyata reaction** (commonly Suzuki coupling) is the palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between an organoboron reagent and an organic halide (or triflate) in the presence of a base to form a carbon-carbon bond.

$$\text{R-BX}_2 + \text{R'-X'} \xrightarrow{\text{Pd catalyst, Base}} \text{R-R'} + \text{Byproducts}$$

**Mechanism Steps:**
1. **Oxidative Addition:** Palladium(0) inserts into the carbon-halogen bond of the organic halide to form an organopalladium(II) complex.
2. **Transmetallation:** In the presence of a base, the organoboron compound reacts with the palladium complex, transferring the organic group (R) from boron to palladium.
3. **Reductive Elimination:** The cis-di-organopalladium complex undergoes reductive elimination to form the coupled bi-aryl/alkyl product and regenerates the active $\text{Pd}(0)$ catalyst.
